pageCache.pageTitle: Activity Place Hosts First Creative Workshop Day | Chailey Heritage Foundation
pageCache.text:
Customers at The Activity Place recently enjoyed the charity's first-ever workshop day, bringing creativity, self-expression and sensory experiences together in a fun jungle-themed event.
Throughout the day, participants prepared for a special jungle-inspired performance by taking part in a range of interactive workshops. Customers were able to choose from music, drama, dance and art sessions, giving everyone the opportunity to explore different creative activities and develop new skills.
Each workshop played a part in bringing the jungle theme to life, with participants working together to create performances and artwork ready for the stage.
The workshops encouraged creativity, collaboration and confidence, while providing opportunities for customers to express themselves in ways that suited them best.
The successful event marks the beginning of more creative opportunities at The Activity Place, with similar workshop days planned for the future.
Keep an eye out for more exciting events and activities coming soon to The Activity Place💜
Parent Hub

pageCache.pageTitle: Two dads take on extraordinary challenge in memory of their daughters | Chailey Heritage Foundation
pageCache.text:
Two fathers who lost their daughters just six weeks apart are preparing to take on an incredible fundraising challenge in their memory.
Matt Vince, a long-time supporter of Chailey Heritage Foundation, and Marcellus Edmonds will be joined by 10 friends this September to take on Carry The Load. Together, they'll hike 50km across the South Downs while carrying all the equipment needed to complete 11 gruelling workouts along the route.
Matt's daughter, Luna-Rose Vince, sadly passed away in 2022 aged three. During her early years, Luna-Rose attended Aquamovers at Chailey Heritage Foundation. Marcellus's daughter, Jemima Rebekah Edmonds, passed away aged eight following an asthma attack. Jemima was cared for by Evelina London Children's Hospital in her final days.
To honour their daughters, the team will carry a rowing machine, barbell, weight plates and other equipment for the entire challenge. Every 5km, they will stop and complete a full workout before continuing on their journey, including through the night to finish within 24 hours.
One workout alone includes 400 squats, 400 deadlifts and 400 bench presses.
Funds raised will be split equally between Chailey Heritage Foundation and Evelina London Children's Charity, helping both organisations continue supporting children and families when they need it most.
Matt has already raised more than £50,000 for Chailey Heritage Foundation through previous fundraising challenges, including the Brighton Marathon and the Three Peaks Ultra Challenge. This year's challenge is his toughest yet.
"Chailey Heritage Foundation is the most amazing charity and it means so much to me and my family. The help they gave to me, my wife Sam and, most importantly, to Luna-Rose was incredible."

pageCache.pageTitle: The history of Chailey Heritage Foundation | Chailey Heritage Foundation
pageCache.text:
Chailey Heritage Foundation was founded in 1903 by Grace Kimmins, who was passionate about helping children with disabilities. At that time it was known as The Heritage Craft Schools and Hospitals for Crippled Children.
Grace took over a former parish workhouse in rural East Sussex and brought with her seven disabled children from East London to their 'place in the country.'
In this beautiful and tranquil setting they could be cared for, medically treated and educated in what became the first purpose-built school for children with disabilities in this country.
As the foundation grew, Grace secured patronage of royalty, aristocracy, affluent businessmen and the press to help finance additional building work through appeals or gifts.
Over the decades Chailey has evolved to meet the changing needs of each generation of disabled young people, including those affected by conditions such as s tuberculosis, rickets, polio and those affected by the drug Thalidomide. During both World Wars, injured soldiers were brought here to be treated.

pageCache.pageTitle: Safeguarding at Chailey | Chailey Heritage Foundation
pageCache.text:
We are committed to the safeguarding of children, young people, and adults in our care.
Chailey Heritage Foundation has long been a champion in the field of safeguarding children and young people with disabilities.
'Safeguarding Children and Adults at Risk' includes 'Child Protection'.
Chailey Heritage Foundation’s statutory duties under Working Together to Safeguard Children 2023, Care Standards Act 2000, Children Act 1989 amended in 2004 and the Care Act 2014, to protect and safeguard all children and young people here, are met through a number of internal policies and procedures, mandatory training and protocols.
All Chailey Heritage School colleagues have read and are trained on 'Keeping Children Safe in Education'.
A team of colleagues (pictured below) are specially trained Designated Safeguarding Leads (DSLs) for our organisation and there is also a named Safeguarding and Whistleblowing Governor.
All Safeguarding and associated policies are available to download below, with paper versions available upon request.

pageCache.pageTitle: Dervia Sensory Suite Opening | Chailey Heritage Foundation
pageCache.text:
We opened the new Dervia Sensory Studio, a purpose‑built space designed to enhance learning, development and wellbeing for children and young people at the school.
Funded by the Dervia Foundation, the studio opened in February and now offers three individual sensory rooms created by our specialist team. Each room provides a carefully designed environment where pupils can explore sound, light, movement and texture in ways that support their education, sensory needs and development goals.
These new spaces will allow children and young people to learn, communicate and express themselves in ways that are right for them. They also give our therapists and teachers greater flexibility to tailor sessions to meet each pupil’s needs.
We’re incredibly grateful to the Dervia Foundation for making this transformative project possible. Their generosity will have a lasting impact on the children and young people we support every day.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ellis' Journey at The Activity Place | Chailey Heritage Foundation
pageCache.text:
What started as a place to stay active after college has become a space where Ellis has discovered new talents, built confidence and found ways to give back.
Ellis joined The Activity Place in September 2023 after leaving college. Looking for opportunities to keep busy, try new activities and meet people, he quickly became involved in many aspects of the programme.
"I loved getting involved with the gym, games, art and cooking,"
A year later, he also began using the swimming pool, combining his enjoyment of The Activity Place with his passion for keeping fit.
But Ellis' connection to Chailey goes back much further. Having attended Chailey as a child, he felt a strong connection to the charity and wanted to contribute in a meaningful way. This inspired him to take the next step and become a volunteer.
"I started volunteering and loved it because I felt like I was giving something back."
Volunteering has given Ellis the opportunity to support others and continue developing his confidence.
When creative music sessions were introduced at The Activity Place, Ellis embraced the opportunity to explore songwriting and performance. What began as attending sessions soon developed into a creative outlet that has helped him express himself and showcase his talents.
"The Activity Place introduced creative music sessions, which I loved because I began to write my own songs and I currently have half an album written."
One of the highlights of Ellis' journey was performing live for the first time at Celebration Day.
"I was able to perform for the first time on Celebration Day in front of my family, my friends, my students and of course the wonderful Jess, which was amazing."
Through both volunteering and music, Ellis has grown in confidence and developed skills that continue to shape his future.
"I gained so much more confidence from the volunteering role and then writing and performing my own songs. I find it easier to express myself through music and I love everything."
Ellis' story is a wonderful example of the opportunities available through The Activity Place. Discovering a passion for music, his journey highlights the positive impact that the right support and opportunities can have on confidence, wellbeing and independence.
Parent Hub

pageCache.pageTitle: Support Chailey's Farm Animals Through Animal Sponsorship | Chailey Heritage Foundation
pageCache.text:
Animal lovers can support the care of Chailey Heritage Foundation's much-loved farm animals through a range of sponsorship packages designed for all ages.
Starting from just £4 a month, our animal sponsorships offer a fun and meaningful way to support the animals that play such an important role in life at Chailey. Each sponsorship includes a sponsorship certificate, a farm animal fact file and a farm sticker.
For those looking for a more hands-on experience, our Large & Loud Sponsorship package includes a two-hour visit to the farm annually, giving supporters the opportunity to get up close with some of our animals. During the experience, visitors can help feed and groom selected animals while learning more about their care.
Recently, we welcomed Louis and his family to the farm as part of their sponsorship experience. They enjoyed spending time with the animals and getting involved in farm life firsthand.
The animals at Chailey bring joy to children, young people, families and visitors throughout the year. Sponsorships help support their care and wellbeing, ensuring they continue to thrive and provide valuable experiences for everyone who visits.
Whether you're looking for a unique gift or a way to support Chailey Heritage Foundation, sponsoring a farm animal is a wonderful way to help support us!

At Chailey Heritage Foundation, we support children and young people with complex disabilities, and their families. Together, we nurture their potential and help them to explore what's possible.
This life-changing work is only possible because of the passionate, skilled and caring people who make up our team. Whether you’re working directly with the young people we support, keeping things running smoothly behind the scenes, or helping us grow our reach and impact, you’ll be part of something that really matters.

pageCache.pageTitle: Who we are | Chailey Heritage Foundation
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Chailey Heritage Foundation!
Chailey Heritage Foundation is a charity that supports children and young people with complex disabilities, and their families.
We're here to listen, nurture their potential, and create life-changing opportunities, together.
About us
Living with complex disabilities can be overwhelming and isolating.
Our charity is here for children and young people living with multiple physical, medical and communication needs. We’re here to listen and explore life-changing possibilities together.
Our outstanding school, welcoming residential homes and bustling centre combining gym and art therapy, a farm and café create a thriving community of support. Our expert team dedicate time, patience and curiosity to nurturing the potential of every child and young person who comes to us.
By sharing our skills and expertise within and beyond our sector, more children and young people are able to benefit from our approaches.
- Welcome to Chailey Heritage Foundation

As a thriving community of support for children, young people and families living with complex disabilities, we're here to listen and to explore life-changing possibilities, together.
Our staff and volunteers are passionate about what they do and they dedicate time, patience and curiosity to nurturing the potential of every child and young person at Chailey - whether they attend our school, live in one of our residential homes or attend a holiday club.
Every day at Chailey is an opportunity to explore potential - and have fun!

Charitable Objects
The objects of the Charity are, for the public benefit, the education and care of people who have physical disabilities and other complex health needs, particularly but not exclusively children and young persons (the beneficiaries) including the conduct and maintenance of a special school (the School) within the meaning of the Education Acts and of a transition service for beneficiaries.
The Board of Trustees
The Board of Trustees has overall control of the Charity, its property and funds, and meet as a full Board at least three times a year. They are supported by a Board of Governors with delegated powers in accordance with the Scheme of Delegation and both boards operate through a sub-committee structure (shown below).

HRH The Duchess of Gloucester
Our President
We are very sad that our President, Verena Hanbury, passed away peacefully at home on 30th May 2026. Verena was the granddaughter of our Founder, Dame Grace Kimmins, and was involved with the charity as a child when she visited her grandmother here on site. She became a Governor in 1962 and was Chair of Governors from 1968 to 2004 when she became a Trustee. Verena remained a Trustee until she retired in 2018. Chailey Heritage was always very close to Verena’s heart, and she kept up with everything going on here, even when she moved from the family home in Piltdown to Gloucestershire. Our thoughts are very much with Verena’s family and loved ones at this sad time, especially Lucinda Baker and Charlie Kimmins, both former Trustees and now Honorary Vice-Presidents.

Governor Training, Focus Visits and Attendance
Effectiveness surveys and skills audits are carried out by both the Trustee and Governing Board, alongside training and regular Governor/Trustee visits to the services. Governor attendance is reported annually.
The Chief Executive provides a strategy update and performance digest at each Board Meeting. The Trustees are alerted to new Charity Commission guidance, other relevant alerts and to new regulatory requirements with training provided as required.

Appointments
Newly appointed Trustees and Governors are selected through an open process of advertisement, application and interview and managed by an Appointments Committee. This committee meets as required and also oversees the appointment of the Chief Executive and other key senior executives.
The election of parent and staff Governors is overseen by the Chair of the Board of Governors and the process is carried out by the Governance Manager.
There is a Governance Handbook for Governors and Trustees, together with a thorough induction programme for new Trustees and Governors.
An enhanced DBS check is required for all Governor and Trustee appointments. An annual declaration of interests’ form is completed and Governors and Trustees are expected to declare their interest in any item on the agenda of a committee meeting.

pageCache.text:
Increase our reach and impact
Our new five-year strategy (2024-2029) is all about increasing our reach and impact. We will continue to be evidence-led and seek to forge alliances within and beyond our sector to make the biggest difference possible.
In seeking to make this difference, we will continue to grow our services and share our skills and expertise with others. We will amplify the voices of children, young people and their families to influence policy-makers to better consider their needs, so that barriers to achieving potential are removed.

Fuego Lounge community raises more than £6,400 for Chailey Heritage Foundation
Chailey Heritage Foundation is celebrating the incredible support of Fuego Lounge and its local community after they raised an amazing amount through the LoungeAid fundraising campaign.
Throughout the year, customers, employees and supporters came together to take part in a wide range of fundraising activities. From quiz nights and bake sales to charity football matches and even skydives, the community went above and beyond to raise funds for children and young people!
Everyone at Chailey Heritage Foundation would like to say a heartfelt thank you to Fuego Lounge and everyone who took part in the fundraising activities.
Thank you to everyone involved for helping us continue supporting children and young people to live their lives to the fullest 💜

pageCache.text:
Our Innovative CHILD Curriculum
The Chailey Heritage Individual Learner Driven (CHILD) Curriculum is a bespoke curriculum created to accommodate each individual’s learning needs.
The CHILD Curriculum covers eight key areas:
Alongside each learner’s journeys, we also have a busy calendar of events, from Harvest Festival to our end-of-year Celebration Day. Pupils enjoy sensory sessions themed around holidays like Easter, Christmas, and Diwali, helping them engage with the world around them. Supported by teachers and education assistants, they also make seasonal gifts, join workshops with local drama and music groups, and go on school trips.
Physical activity is not an add-on to the curriculum, it's an essential part of the curriculum
All pupils at Chailey have some level of difficulty with communication. We believe that every individual has a need and a right to communicate.
Working closely with Speech and Language Therapists, we develop a wide variety of Alternative and Augmentative Communication (AAC) approaches to meet the individual needs of our pupils. These range from subtle body language and sensory cues to advanced communication technologies.
Specialist techniques and resources include:
As part of their curriculum, all pupils at Chailey can take part in our extensive physical programme. Working closely with Physiotherapists and Occupational Therapists, a bespoke physical activity programme is developed for each student.
Every young person has the opportunity to experience appropriate forms of powered mobility. Our award-winning engineering team have developed a range of advanced assistive technologies to develop driving skills and aid independence.
We have a dedicated Engineering and Assistive Technology department who work on innovative solutions to help pupils interact with their environment and provide them with new control opportunities, as well as enabling them to move around independently.
Working in partnership with the Rehabilitation Engineering Services team at Chailey Heritage Clinical Services allows us to:
